hypotheses.title: Memory limit cut to 256Mi gets payments-api killed for running out of memory
hypotheses.summary: payments-api in prod-eu-west is killed by the kernel when it exceeds its memory limit, which the latest release lowered (payments-api memory limit 512Mi → 256Mi). Each kill restarts the container, and repeated restarts put it in CrashLoopBackOff, so callers see refused connections.

evidence.text: payments-api containers were killed for running out of memory (OOMKilled, 5 records from Kubernetes and the kernel, first at 21:50:00 UTC), exit code 137, memory limit 256Mi, 6 restarts so far.
Helm lowered the memory limit: payments-api memory limit 512Mi → 256Mi (release payments).
Kubernetes reports CrashLoopBackOff for payments-api 10 times — the kill-restart cycle after each out-of-memory kill.
Alert KubeContainerOOMKilled is firing for payments-api.
The kernel's out-of-memory killer on 3 nodes killed the payments-api process 4 times.
The same release also turns on PAYMENTS_CACHE_WARMUP=true and PAYMENTS_CACHE_WARMUP_ENTRIES=1200000, which likely need more memory.
The memory request went down too: payments-api memory request 512Mi → 256Mi.

rollbacks.title: Roll back Helm release payments to r41 in prod-eu-west
commands: kubectl --context prod-eu-west -n shop rollout status deployment/payments-api --timeout=5m
caveats: Helm records the rollback as a new revision (r43) with the contents of r41; r42 stays in the history.

It reverts all of r42's template changes, not only the suspect one: payments-api image tag 2.13.4 → 2.14.0; env PAYMENTS_CACHE_WARMUP added (true) to payments-api; env PAYMENTS_CACHE_WARMUP_ENTRIES added (1200000) to payments-api; payments-api memory request 512Mi → 256Mi; and 1 more.
Hold the rollout of payments r42 to prod-us-east (healthy there) until the cause is fixed.
If Argo CD or Flux manages this release, pause auto-sync first (argocd app set <app> --sync-policy none, or flux suspend helmrelease payments -n shop), or it will re-apply r42 within minutes.
prerequisites: Access to kube-context prod-eu-west with rights to change namespace shop.
Check that r41 ran without problems before r42: helm history payments -n shop --kube-context prod-eu-west --max 5

rollbacks.title: Restore payments-api memory limit to 512Mi
commands: kubectl --context prod-eu-west -n shop set resources deployment/payments-api -c payments-api --limits=memory=512Mi --requests=memory=512Mi
kubectl --context prod-eu-west -n shop rollout status deployment/payments-api --timeout=5m
caveats: Changing resources rolls the pods (a rolling restart).
The next helm upgrade sets the limit back to 256Mi unless the chart values change too; until then Helm's record and the cluster differ.

If Argo CD or Flux manages this release, pause auto-sync first (argocd app set <app> --sync-policy none, or flux suspend helmrelease payments -n shop), or it will revert this kubectl change within minutes.
The same release also added PAYMENTS_CACHE_WARMUP and PAYMENTS_CACHE_WARMUP_ENTRIES; with them still on, memory use may exceed even the old limit.
prerequisites: Nodes have room for 512Mi per pod (kubectl describe nodes, Allocated resources).

rollbacks.title: Shift user traffic away from prod-eu-west to prod-us-east
commands: az network traffic-manager endpoint update --resource-group <resource-group> --profile-name <profile> --type azureEndpoints --name <prod-eu-west-endpoint> --endpoint-status Disabled
caveats: These are templates for three common layers (DNS weights, a cloud traffic manager, a Gateway API route); use the one that routes users between your clusters and fill the <…> placeholders.
prod-us-east must absorb the extra load; check autoscaler maximums and node capacity first.
A DNS-based shift takes effect only as resolver caches expire (the record's TTL).
This does not fix prod-eu-west; roll back or fix it before shifting traffic back, and do not roll the suspect release out to the healthy cluster meanwhile.
prerequisites: Know which layer sends users to each cluster, and that prod-us-east serves the same routes.
